Uprating listed rents - attempt to do this with fixed effects.
Problem: there will be boroughs (City of London likely) with few repeated observations, where the borough-year effects will not be calculated.
Could do instead: something like a spatial regression with an adaptive bandwidth instead of a borough fixed effect?
Advantage of this approach: consistent in a sense that I am estimating what the listing price in a given year would be

```{python}

listings_lad = (

listings_lad["lad26cd"].value_counts(dropna=False) # 33

# data prep
df = listings_lad[["property_id", "lad26cd", "source_year", "listed_price"]]
df["log_price"] = np.log(df["listed_price"])
df["la_year"] = df["lad26cd"] + "_" + df["source_year"].astype(str)

years = sorted(df["source_year"].unique())

# fit fixed effects on rent_listings
model = pf.feols("log_price ~ 1 | property_id + la_year", data=df)
gamma = pd.Series(model.fixef()["C(la_year)"])      # borough-year effects

df["alpha_part"] = df["log_price"] - df["la_year"].map(gamma)
props = df.groupby("property_id").agg(alpha=("alpha_part", "mean"), lad26cd=("lad26cd", "first")).reset_index()

# estimate 2011, 2021, 2024 rent for each property

for year in years:
    props[f"estimated_rent_{year}"] = np.exp(props["alpha"] + (props["lad26cd"] + f"_{year}").map(gamma))


# then merge into spine either: actually existing or estimated rent for the three years
```

Rent inputation

```{python}
len(spine)
len(spine[~spine["est_rent_2011"].isna()])

spine.groupby("oa11cd").size().value_counts()
listings_by_oa = 
spine[~spine["est_rent_2011"].isna()].groupby("lsoa21cd").size().value_counts(dropna=False).sort_index()



years = [2011, 2014, 2021, 2024]
K = 8                  # neighbours to use
MAX_DIST = 1000        # metres; donors further away are ignored

# Recipients: private rented in either census year
is_target = spine["private_rented_2011"] | spine["private_rented_2021"]
print(is_target.sum(), "target properties")

for y in years:
    col = f"est_rent_{y}"
    n_missing = (is_target & spine[col].isna()).sum()
    n_donors = spine[col].notna().sum()
    print(y, "| targets missing:", n_missing, "| donors:", n_donors)


y = 2011
col = f"est_rent_{y}"

donor_mask = spine[col].notna()
target_mask = is_target & spine[col].isna()

donor_xy = spine.loc[donor_mask, ["x_coordinate", "y_coordinate"]].to_numpy()
donor_rent = spine.loc[donor_mask, col].to_numpy()
target_xy = spine.loc[target_mask, ["x_coordinate", "y_coordinate"]].to_numpy()

tree = cKDTree(donor_xy)
dist, idx = tree.query(target_xy, k=K, distance_upper_bound=MAX_DIST)

# Missing neighbours come back with idx == len(donors) and dist == inf.
# Pad donor_rent with a NaN so those indices resolve to NaN.
rent_padded = np.append(donor_rent, np.nan)
neighbour_rents = rent_padded[idx]           # shape (n_targets, K)

imputed = np.nanmedian(neighbour_rents, axis=1)   # NaN if no donors within MAX_DIST
n_donors_used = np.isfinite(dist).sum(axis=1)
mean_dist = np.where(np.isfinite(dist), dist, np.nan)
mean_dist = np.nanmean(mean_dist, axis=1)

spine[f"{col}_imputed"] = False
spine[f"{col}_n_donors"] = np.nan
spine[f"{col}_donor_dist"] = np.nan

spine.loc[target_mask, col] = imputed
spine.loc[target_mask, f"{col}_n_donors"] = n_donors_used
spine.loc[target_mask, f"{col}_donor_dist"] = mean_dist
spine.loc[target_mask & spine[col].notna(), f"{col}_imputed"] = True

print(spine.loc[target_mask, col].notna().mean(), "of targets filled")

spine.loc[target_mask, [col, f"{col}_n_donors", f"{col}_donor_dist"]].describe()

```
